newsitem.title: USA: Dollar soars to new peaks against mark and Swiss franc.
newsitem.headline: Dollar soars to new peaks against mark and Swiss franc.

text.p: The dollar soared to a six-year high against the mark and a 3-1/2-year peak against the Swiss franc on Thursday after the German central bank signalled it was not overly concerned with the dollar's strength against the mark.

Benefitting from doubts about the strength of Europe's planned single currency and persistent weakness in the German economy, the dollar has now risen by almost 9 percent against the mark over the past two months and over 18 percent since the beginning of the year.
And traders said Thursday's sharp advance against the Swiss franc was a sign that the dollar now has considerable strength of its own and is not simply riding on the mark's weakness.

"People are looking at long-term trends and saying that there has been a significant shift in favour of the dollar," said Hillel Waxman, chief foreign exchange dealer at Bank Leumi Trust Co. of New York. "Everybody is now talking about targets of two marks per dollar."
The dollar reached an intraday high of 1.84 marks on Thursday, its top level since July 1991, before ending at 1.8345, up from 1.8268 late Wednesday.
It also surged to its highest level against the Swiss franc since November 1993, reaching a peak of 1.5100 francs and ending at 1.5065, up over two centimes from 1.4855 on Wednesday.

Traders attributed the Swiss franc's slide to reports that U.S. hedge funds were selling large amounts of francs for marks and dollars. Despite the mark's poor performance against the dollar, it rose over a full centime against the Swiss franc on Thursday.

However, the main impetus for the dollar's rise came from Germany's Bundesbank, which ended its regularly scheduled policy meeting on Thursday without any change in its fixed securities repurchase money market rate, or "repo" rate -- the official rate it uses to adjust monetary policy.

The market had speculated that the Bundesbank, which adjourned for a four-week recess following the meeting, might alter the rate, which would have signalled its displeasure with the mark's weakness and bolstered the German currency.

German central bank policymakers did leave the door open for a change in the repo rate during their recess, but refused comment on the dollar's recent strength against the mark as many in the market had feared.

"The Bundesbank did not do anything with the repo rate and did not comment on the dollar level and that brought about a real wave of dollar buying," said John McCarthy, senior vice president at ING Barings Capital Markets.
Helped by its impressive performance against European currencies, the dollar also rose to 116.10 Japanese yen from 115.65 yen late Wednesday.
Elsewhere, the British pound slipped to $1.6742 against $1.6790 on Wednesday. The dollar slipped slightly to Canadian $1.3818 from C$1.3824.
